resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (Sale/Transfer of Ownership)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Penns Grove Housing Office
resale_co.lead_time: Fee is due before the inspection is scheduled. Any re-inspection must be requested in writing within 30 days of the first inspection.
requirements: Home must comply with all Borough building, plumbing, electrical, zoning, health, safety, fire and minimum housing ordinances
All property taxes and water and sewer charges must be paid in full before the certificate is issued
Application must list all occupants (names and ages) and the buyer
Smoke detectors on each level including the basement (top of basement stairs), outside each sleeping area and inside all bedrooms; carbon monoxide detector within 10 feet of bedrooms
Mounted fire extinguisher in the kitchen (listed on the 2021 checklist)
GFCI protection for outlets within 6 feet of water; stove with anti-tilt device; bathroom exhaust fan if no window
Handrails and guardrails on stairs, decks, porches and basement stairs; pool fence at the pool entrance
House number, painted surfaces, gutters, soffit and fascia, sidewalks in good condition; no abandoned vehicles or standing water; all trash and debris removed
Roof, electrical service or chimney certification may be required; heating emergency shut-off switch
Exterior doors may not have a removable key on the inside

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy application, covers the initial inspection and one re-inspection
fees.quote: The $50.00 initial application fee for a Certificate of Occupancy covers the initial inspection and one (1) re-inspection.

fees.label: Each later inspection (a no-show without cancelling counts as an inspection)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's Certificate of Occupancy Application (check 'Sale/Transfer of Ownership'; list the owner, all occupants, the buyer and the realtor), sign the re-inspection rules and ordinance acknowledgment pages, and pay the $50 fee (cash, check or money order) before the inspection is scheduled. Housing Office: 1 State Street, First Floor, Penns Grove, Monday to Friday 8am to 4pm, 856-299-0098 ext. 100.
resale_co.contact_title: Housing Office contact (also listed as a Code Enforcement officer)

evidence.quote: CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY APPLICATION Fee: $50 Due (Cash, Check, Money Order) Prior to Scheduling Inspection

No certificate of occupancy shall be issued for a dwelling unit or commercial institution unless all real property taxes for land and improvements upon which the dwelling unit or commercial institution is located and all water and sewer charges related thereto are paid in full.
Any request for a Re-Inspection must be made to the Housing Office in writing no later than 30 days from the initial inspection.
The Housing Office handles a variety of situations such as Residential Certificates of Occupancy and Land Use Questions.

resale_co.notes: The Borough application (uploaded August 2021) has a 'Sale/Transfer of Ownership' box and asks for the buyer's details, and quotes Borough code section 106-5. The Housing Office page lists 'Initial Inspection and Re-inspection - $50.00' and 'Zoning Permit Application - $10.00' alongside the $50.00 certificate fee; the zoning permit is for fences, pools, solar and similar projects, not resales. Enid Reyes's email is hidden on the Borough pages by an email-protection script; it decodes to housinginspector@pennsgrove-nj.org. The Borough gives no job title for her beyond listing her under the Housing Office and Code Enforcement officers. The 2021 form prints the Housing Office number as (856) 299-0098 ext. 101; the current website says ext. 100, which is used here. The checklist still lists a mounted fire extinguisher; P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state smoke certificate rule, but it remains on this 2021 Borough list. No validity period is stated. The Borough code is on ecode360 (PE0949) and was not opened.

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many business days before closing you apply (more than 10, 4 to 10, under 4).

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, applied more than 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: If you are applying for a certificate more than ten business days from the closing date the fee is $45 dollars

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, applied 4 to 10 business days before closing
fees.quote: if applying 4 to 10 business days from the closing date the fee is $90

fees.label: State smoke/carbon monoxide certificate, closing less than 4 business days away
fees.quote: if the closing date is less than four business days the fee is $161.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'). Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email address is required. The certificate is emailed once the application is submitted, the fee is paid and any required inspections are done. Homes heated by electricity that do not need a carbon monoxide alarm should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.

fire_cert.notes: The State (NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety) is Penns Grove's fire code enforcing agency (registry code S; the state directory files it as 'Penns Grove Township', code 1707) and is marked 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates) on the DCA's July 2026 state towns list; the DCA portal lists PENNS GROVE BORO-001 under the State and not smoke-certificate exempt. However, the Borough's 2021 Certificate of Occupancy packet includes its own page titled 'Certification for One & Two Family Dwelling, Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance', initialed by the applicant and the Housing inspector. It is not clear whether the Borough still issues that certificate or whether buyers also need the State certificate; confidence is medium until confirmed. The DCA online form is the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance (CSACMASPSIL) and no longer includes a fire extinguisher (P.L.2025, c.19). Liberty Fire Company #1 (Chief Ed Brancard) is the volunteer fire company, not an inspecting agency.

other_items.label: Taxes and water/sewer charges paid
other_items.detail: No certificate of occupancy is issued until all property taxes and water and sewer charges are paid in full (Borough code section 106-5 C).

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The application's office section checks for open permits and current taxes.

open_questions: Does the Borough Housing Office's smoke and carbon monoxide certification (page 3 of its 2021 CO packet) replace the State DCA certificate, or must sellers also apply to the DCA?
How far ahead of closing should the certificate of occupancy be requested, and how long is it valid?
Does the Borough still require a mounted kitchen fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
